GARMIN × EMA / EXPLORATORY DEVELOPMENT RESEARCH / 17 OCTOBER 2026

More physiological features.
A fair test of what they add.

From the original feature sheet to 678 transparent candidate columns, participant-grouped logistic evaluation and measurement limits.

01 / METHODS AND FINDINGS

What was planned—and what the data can support.

The original TULIP_Features_Simple.xlsx contains 54 feature-family rows. It is predominantly an IBI/HRV plan, not a list of 200 ready-to-use predictors. The windowed HRV part alone expands to 33 measures × 46 summaries = 1,518 conditional columns; unresolved durations and percentile definitions prevent an exact total.

Before: 91 supported wearable columns existed; Notebook 12 modeled 43 distinct wearable columns across its experiments, with five in its primary 60-minute model.
Now: 678 candidates are extracted: 438 supported observed summaries and 240 provisional PulseOx summaries. These counts exclude context, quality and model-generated missingness indicators.

02 / METHODS AND FINDINGS

One EMA response becomes one traceable feature row.

Immutable development streams→ accepted groups / supported counter pairs→ eight preceding windows→ 678 feature summaries + separate quality→ stable EMA-key outcome join→ held-out participant prediction

All 3,706 responses from 125 development participants remain in the matrix. There are 3,689 valid outcome/context rows for modeling. Seventeen incomplete scores remain missing. The 32 final-test participants are sealed.

Garmin Unix timestamps receive no further timezone shift. EMA UTC is actual local start minus its row’s local-minus-UTC offset. Minute-resolution starts subtract 60 seconds; second-resolution starts do not. Windows are [cutoff−L, cutoff): no future readings or boundary-crossing counter increments.

Synthetic example: local start 09:22 → cutoff 09:21 → five-minute window [09:16,09:21). Accepted HR 60,90,120 at 09:16,09:17,09:18 gives mean 90, sample SD 30, median 90, range 60 and slope 30 bpm/min. Latest 120 is three minutes old. Three occupied minutes do not establish complete five-minute monitoring. An example score nervous 4+(6−cope 2)+(6−control 3)=11 is class 2; those answers never enter predictors.
Executed source and provenance

garmin_comprehensive/{features,extract,augment,models,run,evaluate,diagnostics,verify}.py; config/comprehensive_features.json. Frozen original HR/counter values matched in 326,128 checks; existing60-minute history matched in 11,118 checks. Source hashes and row slices remain private. No source measurements were modified.

03 / METHODS AND FINDINGS

Feature families describe observations—not continuous physiology.

  • HR:30 summaries per window: distribution, shape, endpoints, OLS trend, half-window change, adjacent-reading differences, observed-minute and rolling summaries.
  • Steps/floors:7 supported-pair summaries each. Rates use supported seconds; they are not whole-window activity totals.
  • Co-observation:HR during intervals with zero/positive step increments; not causal activity adjustment.
  • Multiscale:mean/SD differences between adjacent non-overlapping intervals.
  • Earlier reference:48 reference/deviation columns. At each L, history [c−(L+1440)m,c−Lm) excludes the current window; ≥30 observed UTC minutes in ≥3 UTC hours. Standardized deviations require nonzero reference SD.

HR acceptance remains 30–240 bpm with existing clock/conflict rules. Distribution summaries need ≥2 readings/span ≥1 s; slope ≥3/span ≥60 s. Shape estimates need ≥8/span ≥60 s and nonconstant values. Adjacent changes require two original valid pairs with gaps ≤60 s; removing a rejected reading never creates adjacency. Rolling five-minute blocks require ≥3 occupied minute bins; empty bins remain missing.

Separate or blocked:PulseOx70–100 is a provisional percent-like branch. No new real HRV is calculated: beat ordering, timestamp anchoring and quality remain unverified. Respiration exists only in current-survey embedded fields, not a preceding stream. Calories/intensity semantics are unresolved. Proprietary Garmin stress and VLF remain excluded.

04 / METHODS AND FINDINGS

Coverage and missingness constrain the experiment.

Only one response has all supported features observed. Requiring complete cases across the full matrix would make the experiment unusable. Every primary comparator therefore uses the same 3,689 valid-score/context responses with training-only feature medians. All-missing and constant training columns are removed; missingness flags are trained separately. No target or raw sensor reading is filled.

The original five-feature 60-minute complete cohort is also refitted and compared with imputed predictions on identical validation responses; the different training populations are labeled. Quality-only, missingness-only and values-without-flags controls test whether availability explains apparent signal.

05 / METHODS AND FINDINGS

Logistic regression first, with selection inside training.

Targets stay fixed: three classes 3–4/5–9/10–15; Binary A ≥5; Binary B ≥10. These are exploratory categories, not clinical diagnoses. Context is actual-local cyclic time and training-encoded survey type.

Five original participant folds define held-out predictions. Three grouped inner folds choose regularization and feature groups. Medians, scaling, constant removal, correlation filters and encoders are fitted within every training split.

L2 tests C = {0.01, 0.1, 1, 10}. L1 and Elastic Net (mixing ratio 0.5) test C = {0.01, 0.1, 1}. Correlation filtering removes later features with |r|>.95 using training values only. Group selection chooses HR-all, HR/activity-all or full using inner macro F1. Class balancing is a separate sensitivity. No boosting model was trained.

375 unique outer fits cover 25 comparisons × 3 tasks × 5 folds. An initial scheduler listed the identical quality control twice; the extra 15 entries reused the same jobs. The schedule and completeness counter were corrected, with a regression test. No predictions or fit decisions changed.

06 / METHODS AND FINDINGS

Do expanded inputs improve matched predictions?

The full supported feature set shows a positive conditional macro-F1 difference beyond context. Its three-class macro AUROC is 0.499 and balanced accuracy is 0.338; neither matched increment over context excludes zero. Improved macro F1 alone does not establish useful physiological discrimination.

Full versus context: macro F1 +0.091 (95% interval +0.071 to +0.110); AUROC +0.027 (95% interval -0.006 to +0.062); balanced accuracy +0.004 (95% interval -0.012 to +0.020). Full versus original HR 4+steps: macro F1 +0.091 (95% interval +0.072 to +0.110). Full-model high-class recall is 10.9%, precision 13.0%. High-class prevalence is 515/3,689 (14.0%). Full-model log loss is 1.774 versus 0.951 for context, and accuracy is 47.0% versus 58.0%. The expanded model predicts minority classes more often, but probability quality worsens.

07 / METHODS AND FINDINGS

High-stress detection and probability quality.

Binary A’s positive class is PSS 5–15, not the 10–15 high-stress category. High-class performance means class 2 in the three-class task or the positive class in Binary B. Macro AUROC evaluates probability ranking; balanced accuracy evaluates the default class decision. They answer different questions.

08 / METHODS AND FINDINGS

More columns do not guarantee more information.

Many new columns summarize the same readings. SD/variance, quantiles, overlapping windows and historical deviations can be redundant. Retrospective person-centered associations are diagnostic only; their full-record means never enter the models. The earlier 53.5% within-person score variation does not establish that wearable measurements explain it.

Morning asks since waking; Midday and Endday ask since the last prompt. Fixed lookbacks need not match those recall intervals. Sparse or stale readings can satisfy minimum arithmetic support. Acquisition-versus-receipt timestamps, batching, source quality, activity confounding and selection remain unresolved.

09 / METHODS AND FINDINGS

What to take to Will.

The full supported feature set shows a positive conditional macro-F1 difference beyond context. Its three-class macro AUROC is 0.499 and balanced accuracy is 0.338; neither matched increment over context excludes zero. Improved macro F1 alone does not establish useful physiological discrimination. The original plan is now reconciled row by row; unavailable HRV and undocumented modalities were not fabricated to inflate the feature count.

Next: resolve exporter timestamp/batching and quality metadata, and obtain prompt/wake boundary evidence. If a feature-group increment has a consistently positive paired interval, specify a narrow confirmation using the same cohort controls before any new model search. If intervals include zero or favor context, do not automatically expand complexity. Keep the final test sealed until the analysis and measurement contract are frozen.

Ask the provider for the collection/exporter version, timestamp assignment code, original ordered IBI payloads and rejected-beat flags, counter semantics, and actual prompt delivery logs. This report drafts the questions only.

Descriptive point maxima—not selected winners
task view macro_f1 roc_auc balanced_accuracy elevated_precision elevated_recall
three_class full 0.335 0.499 0.338 0.130 0.109
at_least_5 full 0.502 0.525 0.509 0.725 0.839
at_least_10 full 0.501 0.477 0.505 0.155 0.085

These are the largest observed macro-F1 point estimates among the prespecified primary logistic feature comparisons. They are not an unbiased estimate of a selected winner, and no final-test evaluation occurred.

Verification and reproducibility

Existing tests, boundary/adjacency/history checks, train-only leakage tests, independent synthetic positive control, saved-estimator replays, fresh-fit checks, privacy scans and raw-input integrity checks are recorded in verification.json and verification.md. All participant-level matrices, predictions, coefficients attached to estimators and memberships remain ignored/private. No commit, push or provider message.

All displayed examples are synthetic or aggregate. Timing and physiological validity remain provisional; this is not validated real-time prediction or a clinical diagnostic tool.
